title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
blurb: Learns word vectors by predicting context words, made fast with negative sampling and subsampling of frequent words.
intro: The skip-gram model learns one input vector and one output vector per word so that a word's input vector predicts the output vectors of its neighbours. A full softmax over the vocabulary is too slow, so the paper replaces it with negative sampling: a logistic loss that separates the true context from a few words drawn from a flattened unigram distribution. The steps build the vocabulary, the training data, the loss and the evaluation; the capstone runs a full SGD epoch.
